[MATH: {3x + a,|x ≠ 4,; 13,|x = 4]

Content:
The function [MATH: f(x)] seems to have a point discontinuity at [MATH: x=4.] However, by selecting a particular value for [MATH: a,] we can remove the point discontinuity and make the function continuous.

Content:
We can find this value of [MATH: a] by forcing the limit of the function to be equal to the value of the function at [MATH: x=4\mathbin{:}]
[MATH: \lim\limits_{x\to 4} f(x) = f(4)]

Content:
Remember that [MATH: \lim\limits_{x\to 4} f(x)] represents the value that [MATH: f(x)] approaches as [MATH: x] gets closer and closer, but not equal, to [MATH: 4.] So, when evaluating [MATH: \lim\limits_{x\to 4} f(x),] we need to use the function definition for [MATH: x \neq 4.]

Content:
[MATH: lim_(x → 4)f(x)|= lim_(x → 4)(3x + a); = 3(4) + a; = 12 + a]

Content:
At [MATH: x=4,] the function is defined as [MATH: f(x)=13.] So [MATH: f(4)=13,] and we can solve the equation:

Content:
[MATH: lim_(x → 4)f(x)|= f(4); 12 + a|= 13; a|= 1]

Content:
Therefore, to make [MATH: f(x)] continuous at [MATH: x=4,] we need to choose [MATH: a=1.]

Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
Consider the function [MATH: f(x)] below.
[MATH: {3x + a,|x ≠ 4,; 13,|x = 4]

Content:
The function [MATH: f(x)] seems to have a point discontinuity at [MATH: x=4.] However, by selecting a particular value for [MATH: a,] we can remove the point discontinuity and make the function continuous.

Content:
We can find this value of [MATH: a] by forcing the limit of the function to be equal to the value of the function at [MATH: x=4\mathbin{:}]
[MATH: \lim\limits_{x\to 4} f(x) = f(4)]

Content:
Remember that [MATH: \lim\limits_{x\to 4} f(x)] represents the value that [MATH: f(x)] approaches as [MATH: x] gets closer and closer, but not equal, to [MATH: 4.] So, when evaluating [MATH: \lim\limits_{x\to 4} f(x),] we need to use the function definition for [MATH: x \neq 4.]

Content:
[MATH: lim_(x → 4)f(x)|= lim_(x → 4)(3x + a); = 3(4) + a; = 12 + a]

Content:
At [MATH: x=4,] the function is defined as [MATH: f(x)=13.] So [MATH: f(4)=13,] and we can solve the equation:

Content:
[MATH: lim_(x → 4)f(x)|= f(4); 12 + a|= 13; a|= 1]

Content:
Therefore, to make [MATH: f(x)] continuous at [MATH: x=4,] we need to choose [MATH: a=1.]
